attribution: SPL-PNL Brain Atlas (3D Slicer License). Cite: spl.harvard.edu/publications/item/view/1265
Arterial territories: Liu et al., Scientific Data 2023 (CC BY-SA 4.0), doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01923-0.
Cytoarchitecture: Juelich histological atlas (Eickhoff et al.; FSL).
MNI brain shell: ICBM152 2009c (mni.mcgill.ca). Entry-point markers are schematic/approximate, not for planning.
SPL Head and Neck Atlas (Jakab & Kikinis, SPL/Brigham; 3D Slicer License part B). Underlying CT: MANIX dataset, OsiriX DICOM library.
Craniotomy footprints are schematic approximations computed on the skull surface for teaching; not for planning or navigation.

Pathology case: UPenn-GBM cohort (Bakas et al., Scientific Data 2022;9:453), The Cancer Imaging Archive, CC BY 4.0. Scans de-identified and de-faced at source; only lesion meshes and a brain surface skull-stripped in-house (no scalp or face) are redistributed here. NIfTI derivatives curated via the Pittsburgh Fiber Data Hub (data-nih/tcia).
Molecular case library: UCSF-PDGM (Calabrese et al., TCIA, doi:10.7937/tcia.bdgf-8v37, CC BY 4.0); NIfTI derivatives via the Pittsburgh Fiber Data Hub (data-nih/tcia).

Vestibular schwannoma: Vestibular-Schwannoma-SEG (Shapey, Kujawa et al.), TCIA, CC BY 4.0. Tumour and cochlea contours only — patient skull contours deliberately excluded to avoid any re-identifiable surface.
Spine: Spine-Mets-CT-SEG, TCIA, CC BY 4.0. Vertebral segmentations only.

Approaches specimen: composite teaching model. Skull, neck vessels and cervical spine from the SPL Head and Neck CT atlas; brain structures from the SPL-PNL atlas registered into that skull; white-matter tracts (JHU) and intracranial arteries (Mouches & Forkert, Sci Data 2019;6:29, CC0 vessel atlas, doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0034-5) mapped from MNI space. Dural sinuses, flaps, corridors, incisions and trajectories are schematic.

Tracts & cranial nerves layer and Approaches-specimen tracts: HCP-1065 population-averaged tractography atlas, Yeh FC, Nature Communications 2022;13:4933, doi:10.1038/s41467-022-32595-4 (brain.labsolver.org). CC BY-SA 4.0. Meshes derived from the atlas NIfTI masks (smoothed and decimated).
Reference illustrations adapted (resized) from Servier Medical Art (https://smart.servier.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Fibre dissection specimen: BraDiPho (Brain Dissection Photogrammetry), Fondazione Bruno Kessler and collaborators — Vavassori L, Rheault F, Nocerino E, et al. "Brain dissection photogrammetry: a tool for studying human white matter connections integrating ex vivo and in vivo multimodal datasets." Nat Commun 2025;16:9801. https://bradipho.eu — licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Specimen 19 (left hemisphere): 12 photogrammetric dissection stages, manual SLS bundle annotations, and HCP842/SCIL tractography registered to the specimen by the BraDiPho team. Adapted here: meshes decimated, textures downsampled, annotations painted onto the stage surfaces, tract envelopes reconstructed from the streamline meshes. The adapted file bradipho_spc19.glb is shared under the same CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence.

Skull bones specimen (skull_bones.glb): BodyParts3D 4.0 — BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International (Mitsuhashi N, et al. Nucleic Acids Res 2009). Adapted: bones recoloured and assembled; suture bands and craniometric keypoints computed from bone contacts in this model (keyhole placed by rule). Shared under CC BY 4.0.

Cadaveric plates: Courtesy of the Rhoton Collection, American Association of Neurological Surgeons (AANS)/Neurosurgical Research and Education Foundation (NREF). From the “Rhoton Collection Top 100” slide set (images by Albert Rhoton, Jeffrey Sorenson, Kaan Yagmurlu, Maria Peris-Celda, Marjorie Wang, Adriano Garcia-Scaff, Toshiro Katsuta, Carolina Martins; editing by Jeffrey Sorenson, Carl Heilman; supported by the NREF Rhoton Fund). Re-used for education under the Rhoton Collection terms (https://nref.org/education/The-Rhoton-Collection/); watermarks retained; images resized only, outline overlays redrawn from the slide set.
